system_description.narrative_title: Global AI boom reshapes economies, sparks backlash and geopolitical rivalry
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid surge in AI investment, compute capacity and model deployment is remaking industries, labour markets and capital flows while concentrating power in a few cloud and chip providers. That technical and commercial acceleration is generating social backlash, regulatory scrutiny and financial-stability concerns, even as states (notably China and the US) jockey for strategic advantage. The system is open: capital, talent, data and compute flow across firms and borders, producing feedback loops between technological capability, market valuation, policy response and public sentiment.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: abstract systemic variables — compute capacity and infrastructure, investment flows, model capability and diffusion, labour displacement and skill substitution, regulatory pressure and policy signaling, market valuations and financial stability risk, public trust and social backlash; concrete entities and vectors — chipmakers (e.g., Nvidia), cloud providers and integrators, AI startups (e.g., Anthropic), Big Tech R&D units, national governments (US, China, EU), financial institutions, industrial supply chains (semiconductors, memory), and workforce cohorts (consultants, graduates).
system_description.super_system: Global political-economy of technology (intersection of world economy, geopolitics and digital infrastructure)
adjacent_subsystems: Labour markets, education and workforce re-skilling

variables.name: Compute capacity
variables.description: The aggregate available programmable processing power (e.g., accelerated datacenter compute) usable for training and running AI models.

variables.name: Model capability
variables.description: The overall technical performance and functional sophistication of deployed AI models across the economy.

variables.name: Investment flow
variables.description: The rate and volume of capital moving into AI-related R&D, startups, infrastructure and deployment activities.

variables.name: R&D intensity
variables.description: The pace and concentration of research and development effort directed toward AI advancement and adjacent technologies.

variables.name: Talent mobility
variables.description: The flow and reallocation rate of skilled AI personnel across organizations, sectors and borders.

variables.name: Data availability
variables.description: The quantity, diversity and accessibility of real-world and synthetic data usable for model training and fine-tuning.

variables.name: Market concentration
variables.description: The degree to which economic value, customers and infrastructure are concentrated among a few providers in AI-related markets.

variables.name: Platform gatekeeping
variables.description: The extent of control exercised by platform operators over access, pricing, technical interfaces and distribution of AI services.

variables.name: Model diffusion
variables.description: The rate at which AI models and applications are adopted, integrated and scaled across industries and use-cases.

variables.name: Automation adoption rate
variables.description: The speed at which tasks, processes and roles are automated or augmented by AI technologies.

variables.name: Job displacement rate
variables.description: The pace at which employment in particular tasks or occupations is reduced or reorganized due to AI-driven automation.

variables.name: Skill reshaping
variables.description: The process and magnitude of shifts in required workforce skills, credentialing and training demands prompted by AI diffusion.

variables.name: Regulatory pressure
variables.description: The intensity and scope of formal policy actions, rule-making and enforcement aimed at governing AI development and deployment.

variables.name: Public trust
variables.description: The prevailing level of societal confidence in AI systems, institutions deploying them, and related governance arrangements.

variables.name: Social backlash
variables.description: The occurrence and intensity of organized public opposition, protests or consumer rejection directed at AI technologies or deployments.

variables.name: Financial stability risk
variables.description: The systemic exposure of financial markets and institutions to abrupt valuation shifts, liquidity stress or contagion tied to AI-driven asset and business model changes.

catalysts.title: G20 tech meeting — regulatory debate
catalysts.description: G20 tech ministers and officials will debate AI regulation, with the US pushing a 'hands-off' approach likely to shape near-term policy coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US to urge hands-off AI regulation at G20 tech meeting'.

catalysts.title: Brazil accelerates AI rules before election
catalysts.description: Brazilian authorities are fast-tracking AI restrictions and guidelines in the weeks leading up to the national election, raising near-term regulatory action.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Brazil races to rein in AI weeks before election'.

catalysts.title: EU orders AI supercomputer deployment
catalysts.description: Public-sector procurement of AI supercomputing capacity will expand usable compute for research and industry as ordered machines are built and deployed.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU orders AI supercomputer from Bull as demand exceeds capacity'.

catalysts.title: Anthropic–Lambda cloud expansion
catalysts.description: The large cloud deal backed by Nvidia will drive rapid cloud capacity and service expansion for Anthropic, reshaping commercial deployment dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Anthropic signs $35 billion cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda' and related coverage.

catalysts.title: China memory-chip capacity ramp
catalysts.description: Chinese memory makers' breakthroughs and aggressive expansion (YMTC, CXMT, Soitec deals) will materially increase global memory supply used for AI training.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'YMTC aims to overtake Samsung', 'CXMT makes breakthrough', 'Soitec locks customers into multi-year deals'.

catalysts.title: Surge in public tech/AI backlash
catalysts.description: Escalating grassroots and media criticism of AI deployments will increase protests, negative coverage and political pressure on rollouts and firms.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Tech backlash reaches fever pitch', 'How Big Tech Blinded Itself to the Grassroots AI Revolt', 'America can’t win the AI race if the rollout lacks public support'.

catalysts.title: Rising central bank scrutiny of AI risk
catalysts.description: Central bankers' warnings at Jackson Hole and G20 discussions will prompt intensified oversight and possible policy responses targeting AI-related financial exposures.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Andrew Bailey warns G20', 'G20 Warned Of Growing Threat to Financial Stability', 'Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability'.

catalysts.title: Student and workforce reskilling wave
catalysts.description: Students changing majors and consultants shifting roles will accelerate training, hiring shifts and short-term mobility as labor markets adapt to AI demand.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Students are reconsidering their majors', 'Junior consultants called back to office as AI increases need for human skills', 'Consultants head for an AI showdown'.

catalysts.title: Surge in AI-related cybersecurity investment
catalysts.description: Rising AI-driven cyber risk and vendor activity (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, OpenAI Astra) will trigger elevated corporate and investor spending on AI security products and R&D.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'AI-driven cyber risk is top concern for global financial stability', 'CrowdStrike at Fal.Con Day 1', 'Palo Alto Projects Double-Digit Growth as AI Drives Cybersecurity Spending'.

catalysts.title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing with cloud partners
catalysts.description: Nvidia's halt to revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud providers will reshape commercial terms and bargaining power between chip/cloud suppliers and customers.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies', 'Exclusive | Nvidia Pauses Revenue-Sharing Deals With AI Cloud Companies'.
